verdict: Chevron's profit nearly tripled to $9.9B as revenue jumped 36% to $67.8B, with refining earnings more than quadrupling on strong margins and record U.S. refinery runs.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenues and other income were $67.8B, vs $49.7B a year ago, as Brent crude averaged $97 a barrel vs $69

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.82 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $5.28, excluding a legal reserve, an impairment and pension settlement costs

kpis.label: Downstream earnings
kpis.note: Refining and fuels earnings, vs $1.1B a year ago, on higher margins and record U.S. crude throughput of 1.09M barrels a day at 98% utilization

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash flow from operations was $16.0B; the quarterly dividend was declared at $1.78 a share

segments.name: Sales and other operating revenues
segments.note: Oil, gas and refined products sold to customers — the sales line of the income statement. Up 35% as oil prices rose (Brent averaged $97 vs $69 a barrel).

segments.name: Income from equity affiliates
segments.note: Chevron's share of profits from partly owned affiliates it does not fully control, such as Tengizchevroil in Kazakhstan. Chevron presents it inside total revenue, so it is a revenue source here. More than doubled vs a year ago.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Income outside product sales, as presented in the statement — mostly gains on asset sales and similar items. Down 19% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative expenses
opex.note: Sales teams, offices and running the company. Down from $1,524M a year ago.

opex.name: Exploration
opex.note: Searching for new oil and gas, including dry holes.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion and amortization
opex.note: The cost of wells, refineries and plants wearing out over time.

opex.name: Other taxes
opex.note: Taxes other than income taxes — production, property and other taxes on operations — separate from income tax.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Chevron reports no gross-profit or operating-income line: the $13,946M operating profit here is what is left after the costs above, before interest and benefit costs (shown as other expense). The flow uses consolidated net income of $10,048M; net income attributable to Chevron was $9,924M, after $124M for noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Refining carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Downstream earnings — refining and selling fuels — rose to $4,931M from $1,137M a year ago on higher margins for refined products. U.S. refineries set a crude-throughput record of 1.09M barrels a day, running at nearly 98% of capacity.

takeaways.title: Higher prices lifted everything
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose 36% to $67.8B as Brent crude averaged $97 a barrel, vs $69 a year ago. Upstream (production) earned $5,698M, vs $3,302M. Production itself dipped to 3,980 thousand barrels of oil-equivalent a day from 4,086, mainly because higher prices reduce Chevron's share under some contracts and because of Middle East conflict impacts.

takeaways.title: Strong cash, even after one-offs
takeaways.text: EPS was $5.06; excluding a $160M legal reserve, a $110M impairment and $24M of pension settlement costs, adjusted EPS was $5.28. Cash flow from operations was $16.0B and free cash flow $12.0B, and Chevron cut total debt by another $3.5B in the quarter.

oneTimers: GAAP earnings include a $160M legal reserve, a $110M asset impairment and $24M of pension settlement costs. Excluding these and a $143M unfavorable foreign-currency effect, adjusted earnings were $10,361M, or $5.28 a share.
Unfavorable timing effects of $1,580M cut GAAP earnings — mainly derivatives (price hedges) marked to end-of-quarter prices in a rising market before the matching physical sales are booked.
otherDetail: Interest and debt expense of $304M, plus $17M of other components of net periodic benefit costs (pension and retiree-benefit costs outside service cost), for a net $321M cost below operating income.
footerNote: Flow adaptation: revenue is total revenues and other income; cost of revenue combines purchased crude and products with operating expenses.
